document.title: Usama Bin Laden: High-Level Taliban Official Gives the Standard Line on Bin Laden With a Couple of Nuances, In October 11 Meeting With Ambassador (Islama 07665)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret (NODIS)] Milam meets Taliban Foreign Minister Maulawi Wakil Ahmed, the first meeting with a major Taliban official since the missile strikes. The Taliban call bin Laden a 'serious problem' but repeat that the Afghan people would overthrow them if they handed him over. Wakil asks about his treatment in Saudi Arabia and exaggerates that the previous regime invited bin Laden and the Saudis told the Taliban to keep him. Excised.

events.description: Ambassador Milam met Wakil Ahmed, Mullah Omar's assistant, urging Taliban to expel Bin Ladin
US missile strikes on Khost terrorist camps
East Africa embassy bombings attributed to Bin Ladin
Taliban captured the Nangarhar area where Bin Ladin was based and entered Kabul, executing Najib
Taliban moved Bin Ladin to Kandahar to watch him better

GOP official reviewed Taliban proposals to Saudis with Ambassador

Ambassador Milam met Taliban official Wakil Ahmed in Islamabad; Wakil gave standard line on bin Ladin with nuances, called him 'a serious problem', and asked about handling if expelled to Saudi Arabia.
Reference point: the October meeting was the first with a major Taliban leader since before August 20 (the US strikes on bin Ladin-linked camps).
events.quote: OUR FIRST WITH A MAJOR TALIBAN LEADER SINCE BEFORE AUGUST 20

events.description: Embassy Islamabad cabled Washington recommending increased diplomatic pressure on the Taliban, with Saudi and Pakistani involvement, to expel bin Ladin.
US missile strikes on terrorist camps at Khost, alienating the Afghan people per Wakil.
A GOP official reviewed the Taliban's two proposals to the Saudis with the Ambassador.
Wakil met the US Ambassador and repeated standard Taliban line on bin Ladin; the Ambassador urged expulsion.
Taliban entered Kabul and summarily executed Najibullah.
Embassy Islamabad cable sent to State reporting the meeting.
Ambassador Milam met Wakil Ahmed, urging Taliban to expel Bin Ladin within days.
Brahimi arrived in Pakistan for meetings with the GOP and Taliban.
GOP official reviewed Taliban proposals to Saudis with the Ambassador.
Bin Ladin came to Afghanistan in mid-1996, settling in Rabbani-controlled area.
Taliban captured the Nangarhar area where Bin Ladin was based.
Taliban moved Bin Ladin to Kandahar in early 1997.
East Africa embassy bombings attributed by the US to Bin Ladin.
US missile strikes on Khost terrorist camps.

key_claims: Taliban official Wakil Ahmed repeated the standard line that expelling Bin Ladin would cause Afghans to overthrow the Taliban.
Wakil said the Taliban moved Bin Ladin to Kandahar in early 1997 to control him after Saudi Arabia told them to keep him.
Taliban made two proposals to Saudi Arabia: a joint Saudi/Afghan ulema group to examine the evidence and a second concerning relatives of Khobar Towers victims.
Wakil called Bin Ladin 'a serious problem' and asked whether he would be sent to the US from Saudi Arabia, suggesting flux in the Taliban position.
Embassy judged the Taliban risk alienating Arab, Pakistani and Afghan extremist allies if they expel Bin Ladin.
Wakil said Taliban did not believe Bin Ladin was involved in the East Africa bombings.
